children.text: The figure is shown bowed beneath and between horizontal strands of barbed wire, with very little open space around the body. The framing makes confinement the visual condition through which the song’s memory appears. We cannot look at the person without also looking through the barrier. Historical experience is carried as something that still structures how the body can be seen.

A small figure moves through oversized outlined buildings marked with labels and numbers. The person seems almost reduced in scale by the mapped environment around them. By placing an individual memory inside this impersonal spatial system, the video makes a tension visible between lived experience and the administrative structures of incarceration, where a remembered life is carried through spaces designed to classify and contain.
